messages:
chris: Quick sync — I want to lock down the runtime perf OKR hypotheses for next quarter. TL;DR: do we prioritize KV cache polish, quantization rollout, or kernel routing experiments?
maya: +1. need concrete experiments and launch criteria, not just 'work on X'.
samir: customer signal: two enterprise accounts pushed for deterministic p95 latency and predictable tail under burst. they prefer conservative changes (no risky quant).
erica: counterpoint — smaller customers care more about cost/token. quantization moves needle there. we should split by persona in OKRs.
jia: propose 3 parallel bets: 1) KV cache correctness + eviction policy (low risk, high p95 improvement), 2) quant qint8 canary on non-sensitive tenants, 3) kernel routing heuristics for long-context workloads.
luis: for each bet we need owners, clear canary metrics, rollback criteria, and expected perf/cost delta.
chris: exactly. rough owners: maya -> KV cache, samir -> kernel routing, erica -> quant rollout. can we sketch metrics?
maya: KV metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit rate, tail latency during bursts, regressions <= 5% tokens/hr. failure = any correctness mismatch with golden outputs.
samir: kernel routing metrics: throughput (tokens/sec GPU), percent of requests hitting fast path, model-output drift (should be 0), and CPU overhead. rollback if throughput drops >7% or GPU mem regresses.
erica: quant metrics: token cost delta, latency delta, and quality check via eval set (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or custom LLM eval). rollout safe if quality regressions <= 0.5% on eval and human spot checks OK.
jia: ops questions: can we isolate quant canary to hosted non-enterprise tenants? need billing flags and tag-based routing.
devops: deploy-bot: canary env provisioned: perf-canary-us-west, 12 x A100-sim nodes. tagging for tenant isolation is ready.
luis: perfect — schedule: 2-week spikes to build harness + 4-week canaries. total ~6 weeks per bet if parallel.
chris: launch criteria summary (draft): 
- KV: pass correctness tests, p95 <= current -10% in canary under synthetic burst, no correctness regressions.
- Quant: eval quality within threshold, cost/token >= 15% reduction, staged to <20% of traffic initially.
- Kernels: throughput +10% for long sequences on target models, CPU overhead <5%, stable across 24h run.
maya: add monitoring hooks: token-level cost breakdown, trace id mapping for fallbacks, anomaly alerts for sudden drop in cache hit rate.
erica: also add customer-facing notes for dedicated customers — quantization is optional and must be opt-in. docs + compliance review required.
samir: experiments: we should run a small synthetic workload that mimics real prefix distribution, not just uniform seq len. I have a corpus.
chris: owners add precise experiment plan by EOD Friday. include: dataset, traffic shaping, shard configs, and canary traffic % steps.
maya: will do. I’ll include the eviction policy A/B variants.
erica: I’ll draft the quant eval harness and human review workflow.
luis: devops will schedule capacity and wire the billing flags.
chris: finalize OKR framings then we can present to PM review next Wed. one more: rollback policy must include automatic fallback to previous model variant + alerting.
samir: noted — will add automatic KV bypass for 503s so requests still succeed at higher cost.
jia: can we also track cost-per-inference trend during canary and gate on budget burn?
luis: yes, metrics pipeline already has cost-per-token metric; will expose per-canary dashboard.
chris: thanks team. if anyone hits blockers ping me and @erica. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary cluster created at 1965432155 by devops.
maya: added experiment doc link: https://redwood.internal/notes/RT-okr-hypotheses (please comment) :eyes:
erica: leaving a note — legal needs to sign off on quant for EU customers, flagged it in the doc.
chris: ok wrapping — agenda item for PM review: pick 2 of 3 bets to escalate based on customer risk profile. meeting invite to follow.
